'''Albert Jacquard''' (23 December 1925 – 11 September 2013) was a French geneticist, [[Popular science|popularizer of science]] and essayist.<ref>{{cite web|author=Francetv info avec AFP |url=http://www.francetvinfo.fr/sciences/le-geneticien-albert-jacquard-est-mort-a-l-age-de-87-ans_409927.html#xtor=AL-67 |title=Le généticien Albert Jacquard est mort à l'âge de 87 ans |publisher=Francetvinfo.fr |date=2000-02-22 |access-date=2013-09-12}}</ref>

He was well known for defending ideas related to [[science]], [[degrowth]], needy persons and the environment. He was 10 years an active member of the French communist party (PCF).

== Beginnings ==

He was born in [[Lyon]] to a catholic and conservative family from the region of [[Franche-Comté]] (east of France). At the age of nine, he was disfigured after a car accident in which his brother died. In 1943, he earned two baccalaureates in mathematics and philosophy. In 1948, he earned a master's degree in public factory engineering from the French [[École Polytechnique]] and joined the [[INSEE|French Institute of statistics]].

== High-level civil servant ==

In 1951, he entered the French tobacco monopoly [[SEITA]] (which merged with its Spanish counterpart [[Tabacalera]] to form [[Altadis]] in 1999) as an organisation and method engineer. Then, he worked as a ''rapporteur'' in the [[Cour des Comptes|French Court of Financial Auditor]] (equivalent to the US [[Government Accountability Office]]) and as a senior executive in the [[French Health ministry]]. 
In 1966, he went to [[Stanford University]] to study population [[genetics]] as a Research worker. Back in France in 1968, he joined [[Institut national d'études démographiques|French Institute for Demographic Studies]] as supervisor of the [[genetics]] department. 
In 1973, he was appointed expert in genetics in the [[World Health Organization|World Health Organisation]]. He retired in 1985.

== University professor ==
[[File:Albert Jacquard EDE.jpg|thumb|Albert Jacquard in 2009]]
While he was still working in the [[World Health Organization]], he taught as visiting professor at several universities such as the [[University of Geneva]] in Switzerland (1973–1976), [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in [[Paris]] (1978–1990) or the [[Université catholique de Louvain|Catholic University of Louvain]] in Belgium (1979–1981). 
As a recognition for his work, he was awarded the [[Légion d'honneur|French Légion d'honneur]], the [[Ordre national du Mérite|French Ordre national du Mérite]] and the [[Fondation de France]] scientific medal.

== Ethical and political involvement ==

{{cquote|''I have no solution: I don't intend to build the society of tomorrow. I just want to show that it must not resemble the society of today.''}}

While he was part of the [[Comité Consultatif National d'Ethique|French Consultative Committee of Ethics]] (''Comité consultatif national d'éthique'') in the early 1990s, he took a strong stand against commercial use of the [[human genome]].

He was very close to the [[anti-globalization movement]] and regularly came to the defense of illegal immigrants and homeless people in France.
[[File:Albert Jacquard tombe 1.jpg|thumb|Albert Jacquard's Grave]]
He wrote several books to expose his views and share his experience with new generations.
He made a variety of public statements in favor of choosing [[Esperanto]] as a universal second language in contradiction to tendencies in Europe to use English as a second language.
